text:
Talia Benson: need quick decision today on upgrade/downgrade policy for marketplace plans + the exact way we message it in listing FAQs. this is blocking the FAQ + console copy.

Soojin Lee: +1. AWS/GCP reviewers always ask “how do customers change plans / cancel / refunds?” and we need consistent language across listings + docs.

Cole Summers: from billing side we need to be very explicit what we can actually do:
- marketplace controls the subscription state + quantity
- we map SKU/offer + quantity -> Redwood entitlements
- we can’t do bespoke prorations outside marketplace terms

Nikhil Sharma: hosted specifics:
- Hosted API PayGo vs Hosted API Commit are separate offers (even if same product)
question is: can we “upgrade” PayGo -> Commit mid-month without breaking metering / invoicing?

Nadia Rahman: metering-wise yes, but we should treat it as:
- PayGo usage prior to commit purchase is billed as PayGo
- Commit starts when marketplace shows the new offer active (and we ingest entitlement)
No retroactive application of commit.

Laura Bennett: finance view: also no “crediting back” PayGo spend into a newly purchased commit. that gets messy for revrec + disputes.

Markus Klein: field expectation: customers assume they can go PayGo -> Commit anytime, but Commit -> PayGo is usually only at renewal. we should mirror that.

Dev Patel: support POV: we need a canned answer for “I clicked change plan in AWS, why is Redwood still PayGo?” + the reverse.

Lauren Bishop: Dedicated is a bit different because “quantity” maps to Capacity Units. upgrades happen a lot mid-term.
What’s our policy on decreasing CU? if they downsize mid-month, that’s a capacity planning nightmare.

Talia Benson: proposal to react to:
1) Hosted API
- PayGo -> Commit: allowed anytime, effective when new subscription/offer is active.
- Commit -> PayGo: only at end of commit term (customer turns off auto-renew / cancels, we revert at term end).
2) Dedicated (Capacity Units)
- Increase CU: allowed anytime (marketplace handles proration).
- Decrease CU: only effective next billing month (or renewal), not mid-month.
3) Private
- Upgrades (add-ons, support tier): anytime.
- Downgrades/cancel: at renewal (annual).
4) Add-ons (Compliance Pack / Extended Retention / Premium SLA)
- Add: anytime.
- Remove: end of billing period/term.

Cole Summers: generally 👍. one nuance: “marketplace handles proration” varies by provider + offer type. we shouldn’t promise proration in FAQ.
Better: “billing adjustments (if any) are governed by AWS/GCP Marketplace.”

Soojin Lee: yes, we should avoid the word “proration” and avoid “refund” language. reviewers are sensitive and we can’t control it.

Nikhil Sharma: +1. for hosted commit, we should also say “contact us if you need to change commit level” (since commit floor is configured on our side after entitlement).

Nadia Rahman: careful: commit “level” may be represented as marketplace quantity (e.g., $/month units). If we’re doing it as a single commit SKU with quantity, then changes are a quantity change.
We can say: “To increase committed spend, update quantity in marketplace. To decrease, changes take effect at renewal.”

Laura Bennett: and for decreases: we should say “subject to marketplace rules” (some will allow, but we shouldn’t promise).

Lauren Bishop: Dedicated CU decrease next billing month is fine, but it’s going to come up: “I reduced CU, why is performance unchanged?” / “why am I still billed?”
Maybe we say: decrease requests take effect at the start of the next billing cycle and capacity is adjusted then.

Dev Patel: we also need an internal runbook note: if customer changes quantity and entitlement doesn’t update within ~60 mins, support escalates to Eng (webhook retry/backfill).
But for FAQ, we can say: “changes typically reflect within 15–60 minutes.”

Cole Summers: 15–60 is fair. we should avoid “instant.” AWS sometimes delays entitlements.

Markus Klein: premium SLA add-on is special. we said earlier it’s purchasable but requires activation by Redwood.
FAQ needs a one-liner: “Purchasing Premium SLA starts the onboarding process; charges/support terms begin after Redwood confirms activation.”

Soojin Lee: wording idea for listing FAQ:
- “How do I upgrade/downgrade?” -> “Manage your subscription in AWS/GCP Marketplace. Redwood entitlements update automatically after purchase/changes (typically within 15–60 minutes).”
- “When do changes take effect?” -> “Upgrades are usually effective after the marketplace change is active; downgrades typically apply at the next billing cycle or renewal.”
- “Refunds?” -> “Refunds and billing adjustments follow AWS/GCP Marketplace policies.”

Nikhil Sharma: for Hosted specifically, can we add:
“Switching from Pay-as-you-go to Committed Spend does not retroactively apply to prior usage.”

Laura Bennett: yes, that saves us a bunch of billing tickets.

Talia Benson: ok let’s lock decisions + copy guidance:

DECISIONS (policy):
- Hosted API: PayGo -> Commit anytime (effective when active); Commit -> PayGo at end of term.
- Dedicated CU: increases anytime; decreases effective next billing cycle (at earliest).
- Private: upgrades anytime; downgrades/cancel at renewal.
- Add-ons: add anytime; removal at end of billing cycle/term.
- Premium SLA add-on: requires Redwood activation; not effective until activated.

COPY (FAQ constraints):
- don’t promise proration/refunds; defer to marketplace policies
- set expectation: entitlement updates usually 15–60 mins after marketplace change
- call out “no retroactive apply” for Hosted PayGo -> Commit

Soojin, can you incorporate into the listing FAQ blocks? Cole/Dev: please sanity check language for support edge cases.

Soojin Lee: yep, I’ll update the FAQ blocks today and tag you for a quick review.

Cole Summers: I’ll review for “what’s technically true” re: quantity changes + effective dates.

Dev Patel: I’ll draft a support macro version of the same answer so we’re not rewriting it per ticket.

Lauren Bishop: I’ll add one Dedicated-specific line: “Capacity changes may require a brief rebalancing period” (but we shouldn’t imply downtime). will send to Soojin.

Markus Klein: also add a line in FAQ: “Need to move from marketplace to direct contract?” -> “Contact Sales.” comes up a lot during enterprise procurement.

Talia Benson: good call. closing loop here once FAQ updated.
